Antecedent evidence: Detectable or diagnostically sensitive frequency-following response
Datasets and effective sample: ds006036; eyes-open N=76-80 by frequency; closed-eye four-frequency N=76; external active-control anchor L041
Upgrade estimand: Robustness across state/metric and mechanism-discriminating control
Key result: Eyes-open and closed-eye results differed while state ROI window and denominator changed together; L041 showed comparable phase concentration under periodic and similarly predictive less-periodic timing
Permitted conclusion: Response interpretation requires a fixed state metric and mechanism-discriminating control
Prohibited inference: Frequency peak or phase concentration proves endogenous entrainment

Antecedent evidence: High within-recording neural and behavioral reliability
Upgrade estimand: Metric- and aggregation-level-matched association with cognition or behavior
Key result: ds005048 split-half rho=0.838 and MMSE rho=0.085; ds006780 ITPC reliability=0.972 and d-prime reliability=0.931 but adjusted beta=0.058 [95% CI -0.255 to 0.370]
Permitted conclusion: Reliability and cognitive validity require separate evaluation using the same metric and level
Prohibited inference: A reliable frequency-following response is necessarily cognitively informative

Antecedent evidence: Stimulus-locked target engagement and an acute behavioral advantage over a non-rhythmic active control
Datasets and effective sample: Dryad t76hdr8dm; frozen raw-EEG N=35; 6623 correctness and 6472 correct-RT coupling trials
Upgrade estimand: Within-subject-condition leave-one-trial-out phase alignment predicting correctness and correct-trial log response time
Key result: ITPC difference=0.088 [95% CI 0.051 to 0.124]; RT=-27.727 ms [-36.171 to -19.284]; inverse efficiency=-25.856 ms [-35.455 to -16.257]; all four coupling Holm p=1.000
Decision: Not supported for tested coupling estimand
Permitted conclusion: Target engagement, acute task-performance advantage, and condition-level coupling are distinct claims
Prohibited inference: The measured phase response mediates or causes the behavioral advantage

Antecedent evidence: In-sample neural association or concurrent validity
Datasets and effective sample: ds007648 N=20; ds006780 N=109-111; Dryad frozen raw-EEG N=35
Upgrade estimand: Participant-held-out or nested held-out prediction beyond non-neural predictors
Key result: No clear increment in ds007648; ds006780 d-prime prediction worsened and FSIQ prediction showed no clear gain; Dryad neural-feature MAE improvement was 3.874 ms [-0.431 to 8.032] versus the fold mean and -1.024 ms [-3.207 to 1.013] versus baseline features
Permitted conclusion: Associations require separate transportability and incremental-prediction tests
Prohibited inference: Observed association is a deployable treatment-selection or cognitive-prediction marker
